name: Can a garage conversion be used as a home office in Los Angeles without becoming an ADU?

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between a garage office conversion and an ADU if the space is only used for work?
mainEntity.text: What is the difference between a garage office conversion and an ADU if the space is only used for work?

acceptedAnswer.text: The line depends on how the space is built and used. A garage office conversion that includes insulation, drywall, electrical, lighting, and climate control may still be an office if it is only meant for work and lacks full residential features. If the project adds a kitchen, a bathroom intended for full-time living, or other elements that make it function as a separate home, it may fall into a different permit category. That distinction matters because the approval process, utility requirements, and long-term use rules can change. Homeowners should decide up front whether they want a pure workspace or a convertible living unit, because the design path and permit strategy are not the same. In practice, the safest route is to have the builder and designer define the project clearly before submitting plans, so the city review matches the intended use. That avoids costly revisions and confusion during inspections.
acceptedAnswer.description: A garage can sometimes be converted into a dedicated office without becoming an ADU if it is not set up for independent living. Once the space includes features like a kitchen, full bathroom, or other residential living elements, it may be treated as an ADU or similar dwelling unit.
